study: Basso, Casarin & Funari — How well is the museum performing? A joint use of DEA and BSC
method: Two-stage DEA + Balanced Scorecard museum performance
boundary_for_this_paper: Multidimensional museum performance; basic BSC/DEA is not novel.

study: Basso & Funari — A three-system approach that integrates DEA, BSC, and AHP for museum evaluation
method: DEA+BSC+AHP; expert priorities and weight restrictions
boundary_for_this_paper: Already addresses weighting of multiple museum-performance dimensions and preference dispersion.

study: del Barrio-Tellado & Herrero-Prieto — Analysing productivity and technical change in museums: A dynamic network approach
boundary_for_this_paper: Dynamic museum efficiency and time carryovers; ordinary dynamic DEA is not novel.

study: Performance of cultural heritage institutions: A regional perspective
Aparicio et al. — An innovative approach to efficiency measurement: CEAT + DEA to benchmark U.S. museums
method: Convexified Efficiency Analysis Trees + DEA; peer benchmarks
boundary_for_this_paper: Very recent SEPS museum benchmarking; generic efficiency/benchmarking route saturated.

study: Bille et al. — Efficiency of Danish Museums and State Funding Allocation
method: Two-stage DEA-BSC + state funding allocation + weight sensitivity
boundary_for_this_paper: Directly overlaps multi-mission performance plus public funding reallocation.

study: Brzezicki & Prędki — Efficiency of Polish Museums' Activities in Terms of Attracting Visitors and Event Participants
method: Network SBM DEA + Tobit, 174 public museums
boundary_for_this_paper: Museum visitor/event efficiency and subsidy-parameterization context.

study: Cavalieri et al. — Do governance features shape museum behaviour? Insights from participation to competitive funding
method: Governance and competitive funding; staggered causal design
boundary_for_this_paper: Shows funding/governance causal museum work uses stronger identification than simple GIA correlations.

study: Digital technologies and economic performance of Italian museums
method: Near-universe museum microdata; visits/revenue; governance/access heterogeneity
boundary_for_this_paper: Current museum performance outcomes already studied with rich microdata and contextual heterogeneity.

study: Seth & McGillivray — Composite indices, alternative weights, and comparison robustness
method: Robust comparison of linear composite indices over allowable weight sets
boundary_for_this_paper: Weight-set robustness and comparison intervals are established general methodology; cannot claim mathematical novelty from unknown-weight envelopes alone.

study: Yue, Zhang & Lv — Pyramid-Shaped Indicators: Evaluating Robustness Under Weight Uncertainty
method: Partial-order comparison and Hasse diagrams under uncertain indicator weights
boundary_for_this_paper: Partial-order/weight-uncertainty robustness is already explicit methodology; museum application must add policy/data/time-resilience value.

study: Nguyen & Gigliarano — Sensitivity-based weighting method for composite indicators
boundary_for_this_paper: Recent OR literature actively develops composite weighting; our framework should not advertise a new generic weighting algorithm.
